text: Have you ever noticed how saving money feels like a high? That's because of dopamine. I teamed up with Virgin Red to see what happens in people's brains and how they light up in response to saving on a purchase. Here are the results and the science. Every time you spend points on a flight, a hotel, or even an upgrade, your brain's reward system lights up. Dopamine doesn't just fire up when you get an unexpected reward, it also lights up in anticipation of a reward. This means that when you know you're saving money, your brain already gets a feel good hit. And here's the best part, when you experience an unexpected saving much bigger than you originally thought, your brain releases even more dopamine in response to that. Research shows that 85% of Brits get a buzz from saving and nearly 1 in 4 get an even bigger buzz when they know that they're spending loyalty points. the biggest highs come from smart wins like bagging an upgrade or spending loyalty points on something
